cells.tense: The two of you are already moving as one current today, and you can feel the choice still being made.
cells.ask: Tell one person the decision you've already made about them, and let their answer change it.
cells.core:
You know what you want here, and you're not treating it like a mood. Two things have found a rhythm together and you're letting it run — not gripping the wheel, not sliding off. That's the whole trick. What you make out of this is going to look like you, because you're not holding anything back to keep your options open.

Keep it that way by saying the plain thing out loud while it's still true. Tell one person the decision you've already made about them and let their answer change it. A flow that only goes your direction isn't one yet. What you're building stays yours as long as you stay reachable.
cells.sheetLine: You know what you want and you're moving with it.
cells.verb: Choosing one stream, and letting two become one flow
cells.place: Where what you are comes out of hiding and stands in its own shape

cells.tense: You are ahead of the conversation, answering things nobody has said to you yet.
cells.ask: For one day, let the other person set the pace, and answer what they actually bring.
cells.core:
You can see the whole shared shape coming, and you're pushing toward it. Conversations start to run like auditions — deciding for both of you, early, out loud. The connection you're trying to lock in is the one being crowded. The easy version is here: two people talking, the meeting doing its own work, your attention on the person in front of you and not the one you've been drafting.

It doesn't need steering. For one day, let the other person set the pace and answer what they actually bring. Notice how often the conversation goes somewhere you didn't plan. Care that doesn't exhaust anyone is the kind that keeps going.

cells.tense: You are still deciding whether to step through something that has already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about what you want to one person today, and stop before you explain it.
cells.core:
There's a meeting you wanted, and you're not in it. The part of you that picks stopped doing that, and now connections arrive and you stay half out of them. You can see the shape of what it would be. You just won't sign for it. When this works, it's plain: you want something, you say so, and nothing collapses.

Say one true thing about what you want to one person today, and stop before you explain it. Watch how little it takes for your nose for these things to come back online. You don't have to trust your own read again before you speak — speaking is how it comes back.

cells.tense: You are already the one this group turns toward, and you talk about it as if the weather did it.
cells.ask: Name one thing you chose for yourself lately, and say what it cost you to choose it.
cells.core:
You're shaping what's happening here — how things run, what people expect, which direction the work takes. It reads like circumstances, timing, what was needed. The working version is boring: the meeting forms because you showed up in it, the plan holds because you said what you wanted, and saying so doesn't cost you the room.

None of that is missing. What's missing is your name on it. Name one thing you chose for yourself lately and say what it cost. Not a speech — just the pen put back in your hand where it already is. Help lines, schedules, boundaries: all fine, all yours. The trouble isn't that you're steering. It's that you've been calling it the road.
